name: Seefeld in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Olympic Village on the Sonnenplateau – a year-round hiking and skiing destination with a unique mountain backdrop.
beschreibung:
Overview

Seefeld in Tirol is situated at an altitude of 1,180 meters on a sunny high-altitude plateau in the Innsbruck-Land district, framed by the majestic peaks of the Wetterstein, Karwendel, and Mieming ranges. With around 3,640 permanent residents, this traditional market town forms the vibrant center of the Olympiaregion Seefeld. Renowned worldwide as a sophisticated year-round resort, Seefeld merges alpine character with urban elegance, featuring an extensive pedestrian village core filled with boutiques and cafés, the Casino Seefeld, five-star wellness retreats, and manicured spa gardens. Seefeld achieved international sporting renown as a two-time host of the Olympic Winter Games (1964, 1976) and two-time venue of the FIS Nordic World Ski Championships (1985, 2019), offering a cross-country trail network of Olympic caliber alongside welcoming downhill ski areas and endless summer trails.

History

Seefeld was first documented in the 11th century as Sevelt in the registers of Freising Abbey, serving as an essential trading station on the historic route over Scharnitz Pass. The town achieved continent-wide fame through the Host Miracle of 1384: on Maundy Thursday, the haughty knight Oswald Milser demanded the consecrated priest's host; upon receiving it, the stone floor opened beneath him and he sank to his knees in terror while the host turned blood-red. The indentations are still visible inside Saint Oswald's parish church today. This sparked centuries of imperial pilgrimage, prompting Duke Friedrich IV and Duke Sigmund to build the magnificent late Gothic hall church. Seefeld's iconic landmark, the octagonal Baroque Seekirchl chapel, was built between 1628 and 1666 by court architect Christoph Gumpp the Younger in the middle of a decorative lake, later drained. The arrival of the electrified Mittenwaldbahn railway in 1912 ushered in modern tourism.

Getting there

Seefeld is remarkably easy to reach by road and rail. By car from Munich, take the toll-free route via the A95 motorway through Garmisch-Partenkirchen and Mittenwald, joining the B177 road directly to Seefeld. From Innsbruck, exit the A12 motorway at Zirl-Ost and ascend the scenic Zirler Berg (B177) in just 20 minutes. Train travelers arrive at Seefeld in Tirol railway station, the highest year-round scheduled ICE high-speed train station in the world, with direct services from Berlin, Hamburg, and Munich. S-Bahn line S6 connects Innsbruck and Garmisch-Partenkirchen along the scenic Karwendel railway. Regional VVT buses are free for guests holding the PlateauCard.

Tips

Photograph the iconic Baroque Seekirchl church situated on its grassy mound before taking a leisurely walk through the adjacent spa gardens. Nordic skiing fans can explore more than 245 kilometers of award-winning cross-country tracks and a biathlon facility. Take the Rosshütte funicular railway up to 2,064 meters for panoramic Karwendel vistas, hiking trails, and winter skiing, or visit the gentle Gschwandtkopf slopes. In summer, walk around Lake Wildsee and its nature reserve in the Reither Moor to spot friendly squirrels and rare wetland plants, before spending an entertaining evening at Casino Seefeld.
